title: Introduce cross-stage latency fingerprinter and quiet-window alert attenuator
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production SREs see alert noise from occasional short-lived latency spikes that originate in different stages of the inference pipeline (gateway queuing, runtime batching, kernel stalls). Existing per-route percentiles conflate stage-level behavior and cause noisy paging. This PR introduces a compact cross-stage 'latency fingerprinter' that emits a small per-invocation signature describing relative stage contributions and a 'quiet-window alert attenuator' that reduces alert weight during controlled low-volume windows. Design summary: 1) Fingerprinter: lightweight sampler attached to the invocation lifecycle that records per-stage token-timing buckets (gateway, auth, routing, runtime-prep, runtime-exec, postprocess) and encodes them into a fixed-length base64 signature and numeric vector for rollups. The implementation uses reservoir sampling to cap overhead and amortized histogram buckets for compactness. 2) Quiet-window attenuator: a policy layer in the alerting pipeline that detects scheduled or observed low-volume periods (customer deployments, maintenance windows, regional off-hours) and temporarily increases alert thresholds and groups alerts by fingerprint similarity to avoid duplicate paging. 3) Backwards compatibility: emits new metrics and trace attributes but preserves existing spans and alerts until rollout is gated. Checklist: - [x] implement fingerprinter and proto for telemetry - [x] expose new metrics via prometheus/metrics-exporter - [x] add trace enrichment hooks and OTEL attribute mapping - [x] implement quiet-window attenuation policy with feature flag - [x] end-to-end tests + staging canary - [x] docs + runbook updates Impact and rollout: default-off feature flag, feature gated by env var and Linear tickets. We plan a 2-week canary on a subset of customer traffic (10% of production) followed by gradual ramp. The change reduces alert churn for low-volume windows and provides a new dimension for SRE to group similar invocations during triage. Observability UX: console change adds a compact fingerprint column to invocation tables and a new 'fingerprint rollup' dashboard with heatmap and top contributing stages. No customer-facing API changes.

review_comments: Ravi: Can we bound the extra memory/cpu per worker? Reply (Maya): reservoir sampler caps to 256 samples per-second and we track only 6 stage buckets; measured <1% mem and CPU on p3-medium in staging. Sofia: How does grouping interact with existing alert dedup? Reply: Attenuator augments dedup by adding a fingerprint similarity key (Hamming distance on bitvector) and only suppresses if similarity > 0.85 and volume is low. Liam: Add a feature-flag and rollout doc. Reply: done, added env var REDWOOD_OBS_FINGERPRINT and rollout steps in docs/observability/fingerprint.md. CI: initial run had one flaky integration failing on trace-sampler; rerun passed and full e2e suite green.
release_notes: Adds a compact per-invocation cross-stage latency fingerprint and a quiet-window alert attenuator that groups similar invocations to reduce alert noise during low-volume windows. Feature is gated by feature flag and rolled out via canary.
testing: unit tests for fingerprinter buckets and reservoir sampler; integration tests for metrics export + OTEL enrichment; e2e canary run against staging with 48h of synthetic and real traffic; smoke tests on console UI column rendering; alerting policy simulation to verify attenuation behaviour
rollout_plan: Default off. Step 1: enable in staging (48h), run canary job (10% traffic) for 7 days while monitoring token-cost and latency SLOs. Step 2: enable on 25% of traffic and review alert churn metrics for 3 days. Step 3: full rollout if no regressions. Feature toggle via REDWOOD_OBS_FINGERPRINT; immediate rollback flips flag off.
perf_impact: Measured overhead: +0.6% CPU and <0.8% memory on p3-medium for typical traffic pattern. Metric ingestion increases cardinality slightly; export uses aggregation windows to limit high-cardinality churn.
